## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over AoS particle components with a list-based respawn intermediate can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout stores 72 B/particle (68 B struct + 4 B list intermediate). Loop 1 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot); loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B/p (5%); loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41%). The approach fuses integrate+decide into a stride-68 pass, appends dead indices to a list, respawns, then renders — verdict kept in registers. L1d spills at N≈455 and L2 at N≈7281, so all measured N are L3-resident or DRAM; the 41% hot fraction means 59% of each fetched line is dead weight.

## Cache saturation
All measured points are L3-resident (N=10000, 100000) or DRAM (N≥1000000). At q=0.01, ns/p is nearly flat: 24.0→23.9 (L3) to 26.7→26.2 (DRAM), ~10% rise at the spill. The knee steepens with death rate: at q=0.1, L3 holds 25.5→25.7 but DRAM jumps to 31.3→30.5 (22%); at q=0.25, 28.2→28.3 vs 33.8→33.4 (19%); at q=0.5, 33.5→33.0 vs 35.1→34.8 (6%). Respawn's Random.fill calls add non-streaming traffic widening the L3→DRAM gap as death rate increases.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 5.674 ns/p (72 B/p at 12.69 GB/s). This algo never approaches it: best is 24.0 ns/p (3.0 GB/s, 24% of ceiling), worst is 35.1 ns/p (2.05 GB/s, 16%). Frontend-bound: stalls at 64-74%, compute at 12-35%, backend rising from 0.1% (L3) to 3-14% (DRAM). At q=0.01 it's marginally faster than naive (0.93-0.95x baseline at L3, ~1.0x at DRAM) but 2.4-3.1x slower than the winner. At q=0.5 it's 0.95-1.0x baseline and 1.8-1.9x slower than the winner. The gap narrows with death rate but never closes.

## Assembly
Codegen is scalar-in-vector-registers, not packed SIMD. The histogram shows vmovss=26, vmulss=6, vmulps=6, vaddps=6, vmovups=4 — one particle per iteration at stride-0x44 (68 B). The loop loads pos via vmovups (16 B) and vel via vmovsd (8 B), shuffles with vshufps/vinsertps, stores via vmovups/vmovlps. No gather. The death check uses vucomiss (12) with jae/jb — branchy, not select-based. Respawn calls Random.fill (3 calls) with scalar bit manipulation (rorx, lzcnt, shl). The render loop does byte-granular scatter: movzx, add, cmp, cmovae, then mov BYTE PTR per R/G/B. The 91 mov and 28 movzx reflect AoS field extraction; frontend stalls (64-74%) confirm decode saturation.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.93-1.0x of naive scalar at every point and 1.8-3.1x slower than the winner. No packed SIMD: one particle per iteration with vmulss/vmovss at stride-68, and the 41% hot-byte fraction caps bandwidth at 2.0-3.0 GB/s (16-24% of ceiling). Frontend stalls at 64-74% confirm instruction-bound execution — the 5.674 ns/p floor is never approached. The list-based respawn's branchy Random.fill calls and byte-granular scatter stores further prevent streaming.
